# Performance

The concept of "Performance" within this corpus refers to the clinical quality metrics and healthcare outcomes for patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF) in Denmark. These metrics are rigorously tracked by the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK)]] and the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program (RKKP)]], utilizing a series of standardized indicators (Indikator 1 through 8) to evaluate diagnostic thoroughness, treatment initiation, long-term medication adherence, and patient education.

A primary focus of performance evaluation is the timely initiation of oral anticoagulation therapy for high-risk patients. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures the proportion of newly diagnosed AF patients with a [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score ≥2 who receive [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] within 30 days, Denmark consistently meets the national standard of ≥90% [^src2], [^src6]. In the 2023 reporting period, national compliance was 92% [^src2], and it remained robust at 91.6% in the 2024 report [^src13]. Regional performance is highly homogeneous, though [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] frequently achieve marginal leads, with Nordjylland being the only region to consistently meet stringent long-term retention standards across multiple indicators [^src3], [^src9].

Long-term adherence and monitoring are assessed through indicators such as [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]] (treatment retention at 1, 2, and 5 years) and [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]] (annual p-creatinin monitoring for patients on [[doac|DOACs]]). While national retention after one year hovers around 89-90% [^src10], [^src11], the standard for annual kidney function monitoring (≥95%) is generally not met on a national level, sitting at 93.9% in the 2024 report [^src9]. Again, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] stands out as the only region to consistently fulfill the ≥95% standard for DOAC monitoring [^src9], [^src12]. Conversely, institutions like [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] and [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] have recorded some of the lowest 5-year retention rates for anticoagulation [^src3].

Diagnostic and safety indicators reveal areas requiring systemic improvement. [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] tracks the measurement of [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)]] around the time of diagnosis. National compliance sits between 76% and 77%, meaning no region successfully meets the standard [^src7], [^src10]. On a more positive note, [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] monitors the incidence of ischemic stroke among prevalent AF patients. The national standard is strict (≤0.8%), and while the national average generally meets this threshold (0.8% in 2024) [^src13], regions like [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] occasionally exceed the limit, registering incidences of 0.9% to 1.0% [^src9], [^src12].

Finally, patient-centric care metrics highlight significant shortfalls. [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which measures the proportion of newly diagnosed patients receiving structured patient education within the first year, drastically misses the 50% target. National performance was recorded at merely 35% in the 2023 report [^src5] and dropped to 15.9% in the 2024 reporting period [^src13], indicating a widespread systemic gap in patient onboarding and education across all Danish regions.
